name_reason: Name is compliant and accurate: data_fd2_ game-global prefix, chapter domain (set by chapter init/event handlers), descriptor reflects it is a flag. No Ghidra address residue. Descriptor 'init_phase_flag' is slightly generic vs the precise semantic (spawn-placement mode: scripted-exact vs nearest-tile-search), but it is set during chapter init/scripted phases and is consistent with how the whole src codebase and KB refer to it; renaming would churn protos.h/globals.h and 4 source files for marginal benefit. Keep.
purpose: Single-byte chapter spawn-placement mode toggle: gates whether a newly spawned battle char is placed by nearest-available-tile search (flag==0) or at the scripted desired x/y as-is (flag!=0).
logic_summary: Read by exactly one consumer, fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle @ 0x10CB7 (MOVZX byte ptr [0x53AFA]; TEST; JNZ): when 0, scan the battle tile map for the nearest walkable+unoccupied tile (min taxi distance) to the char's desired x/y; when nonzero, skip the search and use desired x/y directly. The flag does NOT affect stat/HP/AP computation or any other per-char init -- only the placement branch. Every writer brackets a mid-chapter portrait reload (fd2_load_chapter_portraits_and_dump_tmp, which transitively spawns chars) with 'flag=1' before and 'flag=0' after, so the value is 0 at rest. Observed written values are exactly 1 and 0.
element_semantics: Scalar boolean-style flag. 0 = auto-place via nearest-available-tile search; nonzero (always written as 1) = use scripted desired x/y from the chapter portrait-load record without searching.
comment_original_issue: src comment block (chevt1.c lines 2099-2117) was already accurate, precise, and ASCII -- correctly describes address/segment/size, the spawn-placement toggle semantic, reader behavior, the flag=1/flag=0 bracketing pattern, zero-init tentative definition, and byte-only access. No change needed.
notes: Verified READER disasm at 0x10CB7: 'MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [0x53AFA]; TEST EAX,EAX; JNZ 0x10D4E' (JNZ skips the nearest-tile search loop and uses desired x/y from stack). BSS read returns all zeros (zero-init confirmed).
